name: NAMI HelpLine
summary: Free mental health information, resources, and peer support for individuals and families.

sections.title: About the NAMI HelpLine
sections.text: The NAMI HelpLine is a free, nationwide peer-support service providing information, resource referrals, and support to people living with mental health conditions, their family members, caregivers, and the general public. NAMI (National Alliance on Mental Illness) is the nation's largest grassroots mental health organization, with over 600 local affiliates across the country dedicated to improving lives of individuals affected by mental illness through education, support, and advocacy.

sections.title: Who Should Contact the NAMI HelpLine
sections.text: The NAMI HelpLine serves anyone seeking mental health information or support. Common reasons to call include questions about mental health conditions, finding local treatment providers, navigating insurance and mental health services, connecting with support groups, learning about NAMI programs, understanding medications, coping strategies for families, and accessing crisis resources. The HelpLine is staffed by trained volunteers and staff with lived experience.

sections.title: Services Provided
sections.text: The NAMI HelpLine offers free information and referrals to local NAMI affiliates, support groups, treatment providers, and community resources. Staff can help you understand different mental health conditions, treatment options, and how to access care. They provide emotional support and can connect you with NAMI's educational programs including Family-to-Family, Peer-to-Peer, and Basics courses. The HelpLine is not a crisis line but can provide crisis resource referrals.

sections.title: How to Reach the NAMI HelpLine
sections.text: Call the NAMI HelpLine at 1-800-950-NAMI (6264) Monday through Friday, 10 AM to 10 PM Eastern Time. You can also text NAMI to 741741 for 24/7 crisis support through Crisis Text Line. Email inquiries can be sent to info@nami.org. Visit nami.org to find your local NAMI affiliate, access educational resources, join support groups, and learn about advocacy opportunities.

sections.title: NAMI Educational Programs
sections.text: NAMI offers free evidence-based educational programs including Family-to-Family (an 8-session course for families and caregivers), Peer-to-Peer (for adults living with mental health conditions), NAMI Basics (for parents and caregivers of children), and Homefront (for military families). These programs are taught by trained peers who have personal experience with mental illness. NAMI also runs thousands of support groups nationwide where people can share experiences in a safe environment.

sections.title: NAMI Advocacy
sections.text: NAMI advocates for better policies, services, and funding for mental health at local, state, and federal levels. The organization works to improve access to mental health care, fight discrimination against people with mental illness, and ensure that mental health is treated equally with physical health. NAMI mobilizes its network of advocates to contact legislators, participate in awareness campaigns, and share personal stories to change hearts and minds about mental illness. Members can join advocacy efforts through NAMI's grassroots network.

sections.title: Find Your Local NAMI
sections.text: NAMI has over 600 local affiliates across the United States, each providing programs and services tailored to their community. Local affiliates offer in-person support groups, educational classes, community outreach, and connections to local mental health resources. To find your local NAMI affiliate, visit nami.org and enter your zip code. Local affiliates are often staffed by volunteers with personal experience with mental illness who can provide peer support and guidance on navigating the mental health system in your area.
